results.q: If the JSON text is a thousand opening square brackets in a row, does the parser keep descending, or does it stop at some depth?
answer: parse_buffer.depth is a field of type `size_t`, defined in cJSON.c:294 — the code describes it as: "How deeply nested (in arrays/objects) is the input at the current offset.".

It is set by parse_array() (`input_buffer->depth++`, line 1501); parse_array() (`input_buffer->depth--`, line 1567); parse_object() (`input_buffer->depth++`, line 1661); parse_object() (`input_buffer->depth--`, line 1748).
It is read by parse_array() (line 1497), parse_object() (line 1657).

In short: parse_buffer.depth carries a value produced by parse_array(), parse_object() and consumed by parse_array(), parse_object(). parse_array(), parse_object() both reads and updates it, so it also keeps state between calls.

results.q: What happens when I make a deep copy of a tree that is nested extremely deeply, or that loops back on itself?
answer: This is handled in cJSON_SetValuestring() (cJSON.c:460): it checks `copy == NULL`, and when that is true it returns `NULL`, so the rest of cJSON_SetValuestring() is skipped.
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: cJSON_free() — the previous values stay in place.

When it does not return there, print() goes on to call free() with (`buffer->buffer`) (line 1288); internal_free() with (`buffer->buffer`) (line 1288); internal_malloc() with (`buffer->buffer`) (line 1288); failing_malloc() with (`buffer->buffer`) (line 1288); free() with (`printed`) (line 1294).

Consequence: ensure() checks `(p == NULL) || (p->buffer == NULL)` (cJSON.c:490); `(p == NULL) || (p->buffer == NULL)` depends on runtime values, so it may return early, skipping realloc(), internal_realloc(), failing_realloc().

Consequence: update_offset() checks `(buffer == NULL) || (buffer->buffer == NULL)` (cJSON.c:574); with buffer.buffer = 0, buffer = 0, `(buffer == NULL) || (buffer->buffer == NULL)` is true, so it returns early, so strlen() are no longer called.
Consequence: cJSON_PrintBuffered() checks `!p.buffer` (cJSON.c:1322); with buffer = 0, `!p.buffer` is true, so it returns early, so print_value() are no longer called.
internal_free() calls free(pointer) (line 171).
